section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section contains the opening header and date of the maamar.
section.t: B"S.
Shabbos Parshas Vayeitzei,
Yud Kislev, Maamar 3,

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that war is called "krav" from the term for closeness, and that the soul's battle with the animal soul during prayer requires the divine soul to clothe itself in the animal soul.
section.t: "He redeemed my soul in peace from the battle that was against me, for many were with me."
And the Baal HaGeulah explains in his maamar beginning with this phrase
(printed in his book Shaarei Teshuvah),
that the reason war is called by the term "krav," from the language of closeness (kiruv)
(even though war is the opposite of closeness),
is,
that the essence of war is that each of the two combatants wants to defeat the other and subdue him so that he will be included within him,
and in order to effect this, that he fights against him so that he will be included within him,
it is specifically through the closeness that he draws near to him,
"krav" from the language of closeness.
And similarly, in the war of the divine soul and the animal soul,
the main war is during the time of prayer
(the time of prayer is the time of battle),
so that in order for the service
(prayer)
of the divine soul to affect the animal soul so that it becomes included in the divine soul
[meaning that the animal soul will also have love of G-d,
"with all your heart, with both your inclinations"],
it is through the divine soul clothing itself in the animal soul,
that the contemplation of the divine soul is in such matters and in such a manner that the animal soul can also grasp them.
However, when prayer is from the aspect of the soul itself,
it does not affect the animal soul,
as explained in the maamar.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the refinement of the animal soul through the divine soul clothing itself is a matter of war, whereas "He redeemed my soul in peace" refers to redemption through the revelation of a supernal light that nullifies the animal soul's desires without war.
section.t: Now, the refinement of the animal soul through the divine soul clothing itself in the animal soul,
is a matter of war,
as above.
For the essence of war is,
that there is an opponent and one must fight with him.
And the matter of "He redeemed my soul in peace" is that the redemption of the divine soul from the exile of the animal soul is not in a manner of war,
but rather,
that through the revelation of a supernal light, the desires of the animal soul are nullified,
so that there is no need for war at all.
And as explained in many places,
and also in the aforementioned maamar,
regarding the refinement through engaging in Torah,
which is not in the way of war
(meaning that there is an opponent but one defeats him through war,
but rather)
that through the revelation of the light of Torah, it is the nullification of evil in its very essence.
And similarly in prayer,
that through the love that is beyond reason and intellect, from the aspect of Chayah and Yechidah, the desires of the animal soul are nullified,
and the redemption of the divine soul from the exile of the animal soul is in a manner of peace,
"He redeemed my soul in peace."

section.sectionSummaryBrief: It explains that the true meaning of "He redeemed my soul in peace" is specifically through the revelation of the Yechidah.
section.t: And it is explained there,
that the true essence of the matter of "He redeemed my soul in peace" is specifically through the revelation of the Yechidah.

For the nullification of the desires of the Nefesh HaBahamis through the love that is above reason and intellect, which comes from the encompassing light of the Chayah, is only because the desire of the Nefesh HaElokis
(of the level of Chayah)
overpowers the desire of the Nefesh HaBahamis.
[Rather, due to the force of the desire of the Nefesh HaElokis, the desires of the Nefesh HaBahamis are automatically nullified.
For in the service that is based on reason and intellect, which is from the level of Nefesh-Ruach-Neshamah,
the clarification of the Nefesh HaBahamis is through the Nefesh HaElokis clothing itself in the Nefesh HaBahamis and doing battle with it,
but this is not the case with the level of Chayah,
where through the force of the desire of the Nefesh HaElokis
(a desire that is above reason),
they are nullified
(the desires of the Nefesh HaBahamis)
automatically.
However, their nullification is only due to the overpowering of the Nefesh HaElokis,
and not that they are nullified in their very essence].
Therefore, this is not the true aspect of peace.
And the true essence of the matter of "He redeemed my soul in peace" is through the revelation of the Yechidah.
For since the level of Yechidah has no opposite in the side of impurity,
the slightest reflection of it has no hold there,
therefore,
the nullification of the desires of the Nefesh HaBahamis through the revelation of the Yechidah is
(not that through the revelation of the Yechidah a nullification of desires is brought about,
but rather)
that from the perspective of the Yechidah, there is no place from the outset for alien desires.
And this is "He redeemed my soul in peace... for many were with me,"
that "for many were with me" is the reason
(because)
for "He redeemed my soul in peace,"
for the service of "for many were with me" is the arousal and revelation of the Yechidah
(as is explained at length in the maamar),
and through the revelation of the Yechidah,
the redemption of the Nefesh HaElokis is in a manner of peace,
"He redeemed my soul in peace."

section.sectionSummaryBrief: It questions how after the revelation of the Yechidah, where there is no place for opponents, the Nefesh HaElokis still needs redemption, and explains that this refers to one at a low level who contemplates the Yechidah.
section.t: And it needs to be understood,
that since through the revelation of the Yechidah
(the service of "for many were with me")
there is no place for opponents,
then there is no need at that time for redemption,
and from the fact that "for many were with me" is the reason for "He redeemed my soul in peace"
[for a reason is the cause that precedes the matter which is caused by it],
it implies
that even after the matter of "for many were with me"
(the revelation of the Yechidah)
the Nefesh HaElokis still needs redemption
(except that the redemption is in peace).
And even more so,
from the fact that "for many were with me" is the reason for "He redeemed my soul in peace from the battle against me,"
it implies
that in addition to the fact that even after the matter of "for many were with me" the Nefesh HaElokis
(my soul)
needs redemption
(in general),
it also needs redemption from the wars that are against it.
And at first glance,
even when the Nefesh HaBahamis is like one asleep
(so that afterwards it can awaken again)
it does not actively wage war against the Nefesh HaElokis,
and certainly
when the desires of the Nefesh HaBahamis are nullified
(through the desire of the Nefesh HaElokis of the level of Chayah),
how can it be that even after the revelation of the Yechidah
("for many were with me"),
when there is no place at all for the desires of the Nefesh HaBahamis,
the Nefesh HaElokis needs redemption from the wars that are against it?
And the explanation can be said,
that this that is said "for many were with me"
[from which it is implied
(as above)
that "He redeemed... from the battle against me" is after "for many were with me"]
is in order to hint,
that even one who is on a low level,
whose Nefesh HaElokis
(not only the level of Yechidah,
but the Nefesh HaElokis in general)
is in concealment,
to the extent that the Nefesh HaBahamis wages war against his Nefesh HaElokis,
nevertheless,
through thought about the matter of the Yechidah
[and the decision that his conduct will be in accordance with the level of Yechidah in his soul],
"for many were with me,"
the redemption of his Nefesh HaElokis from the wars of the Nefesh HaBahamis
("He redeemed my soul from the battle against me")
is in a manner of peace.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: It connects the two types of peace, from above downward and from below upward, to Yaakov's journey and the verse "And all your children shall be taught of Hashem, and great shall be the peace of your children."
section.t: And this will be understood by prefacing what is said
(in our Torah portion)
"And I will return in peace to my father's house,"
and the Baal HaGeulah explains,
that Yaakov's journey to Charan was in order to clarify the sparks that were there,
and this is what he said, "And I will return in peace to my father's house,"
that the clarification of the sparks and their return
(their restoration)
to their source
("to my father's house")
will be in a manner of peace.
And the maamar adds,
that the meaning of "in peace" is two kinds of peace,
peace from above downward and peace from below upward.
And it can be said similarly regarding the word "in peace" in the verse "He redeemed my soul in peace,"
that "in peace" is two kinds of peace,
from above downward and from below upward.
And this can be connected with the verse
"And all your children shall be taught of Hashem, and great shall be the peace of your children,"
that it can be said,
that the matter of the multiplicity of peace
("and great shall be the peace"),
a multiplicity is no less than two,
is two levels of peace,
peace from above downward and peace from below upward.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section questions how the maamar can speak of "peace" in both the top-down and bottom-up modes of refinement, when the bottom-up mode is usually associated with struggle.
section.t: And seemingly it must be said,
that the intent
(in the maamar)
in "from above to below" and "from below to above" is
(also)
for the two manners in the matter of the refinements
(the matter of "and I will return,"
the return of the sparks to their source),
refinement in the manner of from above to below and refinement in the manner of from below to above.
And it must be understood,
behold it is explained in many places
[and also in the aforementioned maamar
(beginning with the words "Padeh b'Shalom")
that the Master of the Redemption,
brought above in sections alef-beit],
that the matter of peace is in the refinement in the manner of from above to below
(refinement through the revelation of light),
but not so the refinement in the manner of from below to above
(refinement in the manner of enclothing)
is in a manner of war,
and from this that it says that the explanation of "b'Shalom" is two kinds of peace,
peace from above to below and peace from below to above,
it implies that also the refinement from below to above is in a manner of peace.
And to add,
from this that it is said "and I will return in peace" two kinds of peace
(that both must be present),
it implies,
that in each one of them there is an advantage.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that in the top-down refinement the opposing entity is nullified, whereas in the bottom-up refinement the lower entity is refined through its own will and understanding, so its essential opposition remains latent.
section.t: e)
And the matter is,
that in peace
(which is brought about through refinement)
there are two manners.
That the opposing entity is nullified – and this manner is
(primarily)
in the refinement in the manner of from above to below.
For in the refinement in the manner of from below to above,
where the refiner enclothes himself in that which is being refined and engages with it so that it will desire to be refined,
this is not that the lower entity
(that which is being refined)
is nullified, but rather it is refined from the aspect of its own will.
And since even after it has been refined it is an existence of a lower entity
(for lower and higher are opposites),
therefore,
even after it has been refined,
it is possible that it will oppose the higher entity.
And in the service of man this is,
that the refinement of the Nefesh HaBahamis through the Nefesh HaElokis enclothing itself in the Nefesh HaBahamis,
is,
that the contemplation of the Nefesh HaElokis is in a manner that also the Nefesh HaBahamis will understand and grasp the Divine matter
(in which it contemplates)
so that through this it will come to love HaShem.
For this that the Nefesh HaBahamis loves HaShem
(although by its nature it is drawn to physical matters)
is
(not through its existence being nullified,
but rather on the contrary)
through the intellect of the Nefesh HaBahamis coming to an understanding that one must love HaShem.
And since this that the Nefesh HaBahamis loves HaShem
(including also the understanding and comprehension that one must love HaShem)
is from the aspect of the intellect of the Nefesh HaElokis
(which has enclothed itself in the intellect of the Nefesh HaBahamis),
but the Nefesh HaBahamis from its own aspect is drawn to physical matters
[and as is explained in many places
that the refinement of the Nefesh HaBahamis through contemplation is only in the manner of itkafya (suppression)],
behold even now
(that also the Nefesh HaBahamis has love of HaShem)
its opposition to the Nefesh HaElokis remains in concealment
(except that its opposition does not come into actuality).
And in order that there be a nullification of the opposing entity, it is through the refinement in the manner of from above to below.
For through
there being revealed in the lower entity a revelation of light that is not commensurate with it,
it is nullified from its existence.
And in the service of man this is,
that through there being felt in the Nefesh HaBahamis the love of the Nefesh HaElokis that is beyond intellect and comprehension,
for this love is
(generally)
a great love that is beyond the limitation of the vessel of the heart,
through this the existence of the Nefesh HaBahamis is nullified,
and through this it is transformed to good,
it'hapcha (transformation)
(which is superior to itkafya).

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that in the bottom-up refinement the former opponent becomes a lover, a true change in its own existence, whereas in the top-down refinement the lower entity is nullified but not essentially changed.
section.t: And there is another manner in peace
(which is brought about through refinement),
that that which was initially an opponent becomes a lover
(and in the language of the verse
"even his enemies will make peace with him")
– and this manner is
(primarily)
in the refinement in the manner of from below to above.
For in the refinement in the manner of from above to below,
this that the lower entity does not oppose is because it is nullified from its existence through the revelation of light,
but it is not that a change has been made in the existence of the lower entity itself.
For although through the revelation of the great love that is beyond intellect and comprehension the Nefesh HaBahamis is transformed to good
(it'hapcha),
behold its transformation is
(not from the aspect of the Nefesh HaBahamis's own essence,
but rather)
because through the great love of the Nefesh HaElokis the Nefesh HaBahamis is nullified from its existence.
And the true essence of the matter of "even his enemies will make peace with him" is in the refinement in the manner of from below to above,
for this that the Nefesh HaBahamis has love of HaShem is from the aspect of the intellect of the Nefesh HaBahamis.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the two types of peace (from above downward and from below upward) must each include the quality of the other, so that the refinement of the animal soul and the world is complete.
section.t: And this is “And I will return in
peace,”
and likewise “He redeemed in
peace,”
peace from above downward and peace from below upward,
that the refinement of the animal soul
(“He redeemed my soul in peace”)
and likewise the refinement of the sparks in the world
(“and I will return in peace to my father’s house”)
must be in two manners,
in a way from above downward and in a way from below upward,
through which there are the two aspects
(advantages)
of peace.
And to add,
that the perfection of peace
(peace also from the term completion)
is when the peace
(in each of the two manners)
includes both advantages.
That also in the refinement that is in the way from below upward there is
(a semblance of)
the aspect of transformation,
and that also in the refinement that is in the way from above downward there is
(a semblance of)
the advantage that the refinement is from the perspective of the nature of the lower.
And this is “He redeemed my soul in peace from near to me,”
that also the aspect of “He redeemed in peace,”
which is
(generally)
the redemption of the G-dly soul from the exile of the animal soul through the revelation of light,
will have in it the advantage of “from near to me”
(near from the term closeness),
the refinement of the animal soul itself.
And likewise on the other side,
that also the refinement that is in the way of near
(war)
will be in a manner of “He redeemed in peace,”
transformation.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that through contemplation of the Yechidah, which awakens total self-nullification, both modes of refinement include both advantages.
section.t: And the verse continues “for many are with me,”
“for many are with me” is the reason
(for)
“He redeemed my soul in peace from near to me,”
that through contemplation of the aspect of Yechidah,
through which there is awakened in him the aspect of self-nullification
[namely,
that even before the service of “He redeemed my soul in peace from near to me” and he still needs to redeem his G-dly soul from the wars of the animal soul,
he is awakened to a total self-nullification to G-dliness,
which comes from the Yechidah within him],
through this,
the refinement of the animal soul is in a manner of “He redeemed my soul in peace from near to me,”
that in each of the two modes of refinement there are both advantages.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section connects the above to the Rebbe's father-in-law's explanation that Torah study must be felt as God's Torah, achieved through prayer, which brings peace to scholars and the world.
section.t: And it is possible to connect this matter with what is explained by my revered father-in-law, the Rebbe, in his maamar beginning “And all
your children [shall be] students of the L-rd, and great shall be the peace of your children,” said on Shabbos Parshas Vayeitzei 5689
(in the Kuntres of Wedding Discourses),
that the translation of the verse “And all your children etc.” is “And all your children are learned in the Torah of the L-rd, and great shall be the peace of your children.”
And he explains,
that this precise wording “learned in the Torah of the L-rd”
(even though seemingly this is not a novelty,
for everyone knows that the Torah is the Torah of the L-rd)
is,
that their Torah study is in a manner that he feels that the Torah is the Torah of the L-rd.
And he adds in the maamar,
that the explanation of “learned in the Torah of the L-rd” is,
that even though the study of Torah
(learning)
is that he understands and grasps the Torah with his intellect
(human intellect),
nevertheless,
also in his study
(intellect)
it is felt that the Torah is the Torah of the L-rd,
“learned in the Torah of the L-rd.”
And through this feeling,
also his study
(comprehension)
is in self-nullification.
And in order for Torah study to be in this manner,
it is through the prior service of prayer.
For the matter of prayer is connection and self-nullification to G-dliness.
And through Torah study in this manner
(specifically)
there is “great shall be the peace of your children” – an abundance of peace for the Torah scholars who engage in Torah,
and also an abundance of peace in the world, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, learned
from this verse that Torah scholars increase peace in the world.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: When Torah study lacks the awareness that it is God's Torah, it can lead to divisiveness rather than peace, as illustrated by a story of a scholar who complained to the Tzemach Tzedek about being trampled upon.
section.t: And from the continuation of the topics in the maamar, it is understood,
that when the study of Torah is not in this manner,
then,
(in addition to the fact that it does not bring peace to the world)
it is possible that it will bring about division of hearts,
the opposite of peace.
For when he lacks the feeling that the Torah is the Torah of Havayah,
then,
he takes credit for himself that he studied much Torah43
and becomes a tangible entity that considers himself a man of virtue and an important person,
and this causes division of hearts,
for from the perspective of his selfhood he thinks that everything another says or does is in order to oppose him.
And as the story
(cited in the maamar44),
that someone
(a great intellectual in scholarship)
came to the Tzemach Tzedek for a yechidus and complained, "They are stepping on me in the study hall,"
and the Tzemach Tzedek answered him,
"You are spreading yourself over the entire study hall,
so wherever that one steps, it is all on you."
And it can be said,
that this which the maamar brings, that his claim was that they were trampling on him in the study hall,
[indicates that] although the study hall is a microcosmic Sanctuary45,
for the indwelling of the Shechinah in the microcosmic Sanctuary is akin to the indwelling of the Shechinah in the Holy Temple46,
nevertheless,
even there there was the extension of his selfhood.
And the maamar specifies,
that this complaint before the Tzemach Tzedek that they were trampling on him was when he was in yechidus,
for the matter of yechidus is the connection of the Yechidah of the one entering for yechidus with the Yechidah of the Rebbe to whom he entered47,
and nevertheless,
even when he was in yechidus, he had the feeling that they were trampling on him.
And therefore the maamar brings the above details of the story,
in order to emphasize that through intellect alone,
without avodah,
it is possible for the extension of selfhood to exist even in a microcosmic Sanctuary and even when entering into yechidus,
from which is understood the necessity of the matter of avodah.
And afterwards the Tzemach Tzedek told him the explanation of the verse48
"Let the wicked forsake his way and the man of iniquity his thoughts,"
"on" (און)
(with a cholam)
is strength and power49,
and the explanation of "man of iniquity" is a man strong in his own opinion.
And this is "Let the wicked forsake his way and the man of iniquity his thoughts,"
that just as "let the wicked forsake his way" is something necessary,
for without teshuvah it is impossible to approach the holy,
so too it is necessary that the man of iniquity forsake his thoughts
(the thoughts of selfhood).

section.sectionSummaryBrief: The plural "thoughts" indicates that there are many levels of the thought of selfhood, and even the subtlest thought of a Torah scholar can be a barrier, like a speck of dirt on a garment.
section.t: And it can be said,
that what is written "his thoughts" in the plural,
it is,
for in the thought of selfhood there are several levels,
and therefore it is said "let him forsake... his thoughts" in the plural,
that he must forsake the subtle thought,
and even the most subtle of the subtle.
And to note,
from the statement of our sages, of blessed memory50,
regarding the matter of a speck on a garment that interposes regarding immersion,
that [a speck] of a builder
[these are Torah scholars who engage in the building of the world]
[interposes] on one side, and of a boor on two sides.
For from this it is understood also regarding a spiritual speck,
that in a Torah scholar even a subtle thought interposes,
and therefore it is necessary that he forsake "his thoughts" in the plural.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: The beginning of avodah is self-nullification, which enables both the upward approach through prayer and the downward approach through Torah study, and the peace of Torah scholars includes the peace of prayer.
section.t: And it is explained in the maamar51,
that the beginning of avodah is self-nullification.
For in order to draw near to Elokus,
both in the aspect of approach from below upward to ascend from level to level in prayer, and in the aspect of approach from above downward in the attainment of Elokus in his soul through Torah,
it is through humility and lowliness.
And it can be said,
that this which the maamar specifies the two manners of approach to Elokus,
although in order to explain the language of the Targum "Alfin b'Oraisa d'Havayah" it seemingly only relates to the approach through Torah,
it is in order to hint that through the precedence of self-nullification,
the peace of "Your children,"
Torah scholars who engage in Torah
(from above downward),
is in perfection,
that it also includes the virtue of the peace of prayer
(from below upward)52.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: Since the purpose of the descent of the sparks is for their refinement, there is no obstacle from the sparks themselves, only from the person doing the refining; the sparks desire to be refined, and through the awakening of the Yechidah this hidden desire becomes revealed.
section.t: The explanation is,
that since the intention of the descent and fall of the sparks is in order that they be refined and return to their source
[through which they will ascend higher than they were before their descent],
therefore there cannot be any prevention or hindrance
(from the side of the sparks)
to their refinement.
For that which it is possible for there to be prevention and hindrance is only from the side of the person
(the one who refines),
who has free choice,
but from the side of the sparks – they are compelled to be refined.
[And this is the meaning of what is said, "and Adoniram was over the tax"53,
Adoniram is Adoni Ram (my Lord is exalted),
Adoni is analogous to the Name Ado-nai
(the aspect of the Shechinah)
and Ram, from the term exaltation, is the light of Ein Sof which is above the worlds
(the Holy One, blessed be He).
And according to what is explained below
(section 10)
that the matter of the refinements is to unite the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah,
it can be said,
that "the tax" is the matter of the refinements.
And it is called by the name "tax",
for a tax is something that is compelled to be paid.
And the aspect of Adoniram is that which compels the collection of the tax,
the refinement of the sparks].
And moreover,
the sparks want and yearn to be refined.
And this is "many were with me",
that the sparks which are found in the aspect of "many"
(the public domain,
the mountains of separation54)
yearn that they be refined
[similar to the simple meaning of "many were with me",
that the men of Avshalom prayed for Dovid's victory55].
However, since the sparks are in exile in the aspect of "many",
this is not in revelation.
And even to the extent that sometimes it appears to the person that the matters of the world
(not only do they not assist,
but rather)
hinder him from the service of G-d,
for the concealment of the sparks is a concealment to the utmost,
like a concealment that is as if non-existent.
And through the service of "many were with me",
the awakening of the Yechidah,
the essence of the soul which is above extension
(existence),
the concealment that is as if non-existent of the sparks is awakened and revealed,
and their yearning to be refined,
the matter of "many were with me",
and then one sees in revelation that the matters of the world
(not only do they not hinder,
but rather)
assist in the service of G-d.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: The peace of refinement through the service of "many were with me" (awakening of the Yechidah) is perfect, encompassing both advantages, because the lower one desires refinement, so the refinement is not contrary to its nature but rather a transformation.
section.t: And this is "He redeemed my soul in peace from the battle that was against me, for many were with me",
that the peace of the refinement through the service of "many were with me"
(the awakening of the Yechidah)
is in perfection,
for it includes both advantages
(as above, section 6),
for through the service of "many were with me",
the awakening of the Yechidah,
it is revealed that the sparks which are in exile in
(the public do-)
"many were with me"
(their will and yearning to be refined),
and therefore even the refinement in a manner from above to below contains something of the advantage that the refinement is from the side of the lower one,
for even this refinement is that the lower one wants to be refined
(except that the actual refinement is through the revelation of a light that is above him).
And likewise on the other hand,
that even the refinement in the manner from below to above is in a way that the opposition of the lower one is nullified.
For that which was explained above
(section 5)
that even after the refinement of the lower one
(refinement in the manner from below to above)
the opposition of the lower one still remains in concealment,
this is
because the refinement of the lower one is a matter that is added to it
(through the one who refines that is enclothed in it),
contrary to the nature of the lower one.
And like the animal soul, which by its nature is drawn to physical matters,
and the love for G-d
[that is generated within it through the G-dly soul that is enclothed in it]
is contrary to its nature.
From this it is understood,
that when the lower one is in a state where even before the enclothing of the one who refines within it
(the work of refinement)
it wants and yearns
(in revelation)
to be refined,
then,
the refinement is not something additional to it,
and certainly it is not contrary to its nature,
and therefore its refinement
(even the refinement through the manner of enclothing)
is like the matter of transformation.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: The entire purpose of service is to unite the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah (Sovev and Memaleh), and this is specifically through Yaakov, who possessed the revelation of the Yechidah, enabling the inclusion of both modes of refinement.
section.t: And 4)
Now, it is known56
that the entirety of the matter of service is to unite the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah.
And this is the matter of the unification of Sovev and Memaleh,
for the Holy One, blessed be He, is the aspect of Sovev Kol Almin and the Shechinah is the aspect of Memaleh Kol Almin57.
And this is what Yaakov said, "and I will return in peace to my father's house, and HaVaYaH will be my G-d",
that through the service of the refinements
("and I will return in peace to my father's house",
the return of the sparks to their source)
[for the primary service for which the soul descended below is the service of the refinements58]
will be "and HaVaYaH will be my G-d",
the unification of HaVaYaH
(Sovev)
and Elokim
(Memaleh).
And it can be said,
that through the service of the refinements in both manners
(in the manner from above to below and in the manner from below to above),
and in a way that each of them includes both,
through this,
the unification of Sovev and Memaleh is in both manners,
the drawing down of Sovev into Memaleh and the elevation of Memaleh into Sovev,
and in a way that each of them includes both.
And based on this, we can explain the connection of this matter specifically to Yaakov,
for the inclusion of the two manners in the service of the refinements, in each of which there are both advantages,
is through the revelation of the aspect of the Yechidah,
which is above limitation,
and this is that regarding Yaakov it is stated59
"and you shall spread out to the west and to the east and to the north and to the south",
an inheritance without borders60,
this is because there was in him a revelation of the Yechidah
(as explained above61).

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the Shechinah includes all Jewish souls, and that the unification of the Holy One and His Shechinah also includes the unification of the Holy One and Israel, which will be fully revealed in the future through Mashiach.
section.t: Now, it is known that the Shechinah is the aspect of Malchus,
which includes all the souls of Israel,
as our sages, of blessed memory, said,
"All Israelites are the children of kings."
And based on this, it can be said
that in the unification of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah, is also included the unification of the Holy One, blessed be He, and Israel.
For the perfection of the unification is when it is in both modes,
drawing down and elevation.
And it can be said
that one of the reasons for this is that the matter of the marriage of the Holy One, blessed be He, and Israel will be in the future to come,
for then there will be the revelation of the Yechidah through Mashiach, who is the aspect of the general Yechidah,
the essence of the matter of "and the breaker went up,"
through "the breaker shall go up before us,"
speedily, in the very near future.
